O.outcome_detail: methodological quality rated with JBI checklists

result.effect: Most empirical studies Moderate; three Low; one cross-sectional study High

cells.quote: The 23 included studies, 17 reported empirical evaluations and were appraised with the JBI quasi-experimental checklist, one study with the analytical cross-sectional checklist, and five conceptual or technical papers with the text and opinion checklist (c.f. Appendix 3 3-4). Most empirical studies were rated as Moderate, reflecting clear interventions and consistent outcome measures but typically lacking randomization, follow-up, or standardized reporting. Three empirical studies were rated as Low, mainly due to small samples or insufficient methodological detail. One cross-sectional study was rated as High, demonstrating clear inclusion criteria, reliable measures, and appropriate analysis (c.f. Table 1).
cells.note: The study text does not explicitly state that none of the 17 quasi-experimental studies were rated High; it reports the overall empirical distribution and separately identifies one High-rated cross-sectional study.

D.treatment: included qualitative studies assessed with the JBI checklist

O.outcome_detail: methodological quality scores and checklist deficiencies

cells.quote: The quality of the included studies (n = 17) varied between 12 and 20 points (mean 15.6) on a scale of 0–20 (Table 2). The primary deficiencies were observed in Questions 6 (Q6), which pertains to the identification of the researcher's cultural or theoretical positioning, and in question 7 (Q7), which addresses the impact of the researcher on the research and vice versa.
cells.note: The study is a qualitative systematic review rather than an intervention comparison; no educational treatment, comparison condition, or learner outcome was reported.
